chapter: Decca years and the First Herd
title: Helping young musicians and not asking their age
summary: He says he can help a player who wants help and never asks a young musician his age.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: Do you feel that through all these decades that your way of encouraging musicians has paid off in more cases than not?
Oh, I think, generally speaking, espe-

cially in the last 30 years. I feel that I can help a player if he wants to be helped. Of course, he has to have that kind of feeling, too. If he decides I don't know what I'm talking about, we're in trouble.

But most times, and I think that's the one thing that I'm most proud of, is the fact that we do have a communication, and I still do and I will continue to have as long as I'm alive. And I don't -- for instance, I never ask a young musician how old he is. That comes much later. But people say, 'How old is he?' I have no idea. I don't care, really. That's such a dumb qualification, how old are you. Not, how do you play or -- you know. I don't think it's important at all.
